taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS's antelope bitterbrush review (Zlatnik 1999, read 2026-10-15): "Plants may reach 12 to15 feet (3.6-4.5 m) in height, but usually grow to 3 or 4 feet (0.9-1.2 m)".

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS's antelope bitterbrush review (Zlatnik 1999, read 2026-10-15): "a native, deciduous shrub".

traits.fruit_type.note: FEIS's antelope bitterbrush review (Zlatnik 1999, read 2026-10-15): "The fruit is an achene".

traits.fruit_size_m.note: FEIS's antelope bitterbrush review (Zlatnik 1999, read 2026-10-15): achene "0.13 to 0.5 inch (3-13 mm) long".

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: FEIS's antelope bitterbrush review (Zlatnik 1999, read 2026-10-15): "reaches seed-bearing age in 8 to 10 years".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.inflorescence.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.flowering_months.note: FEIS's antelope bitterbrush review (Zlatnik 1999, read 2026-10-15): "flowers from early spring to July"; at Wenatchee, Washington, full flower May 22-26.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS's antelope bitterbrush review (Zlatnik 1999, read 2026-10-15): "Fruits ripen from July to September, depending on elevation".

generator.params.note: Oceanspray's values, changed by hand for antelope bitterbrush: the common multi-stemmed form, an intricately branched, spreading shrub (FEIS, Zlatnik 1999: "multiple-stemmed, decumbent plants" and "single-stemmed, columnar plants"), with small three-toothed leaves in clusters and single pale yellow flowers. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 1.1 m at 12 years in the open, within FEIS's usual 0.9-1.2 m (Zlatnik 1999). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye: grey-brown bark; small wedge-shaped leaves, three-toothed at the tip, grey-green; pale yellow five-petalled flowers.
